fatal_errors: The proposed 1200–1400°C sintering range is far above the target 900–1000°C window and risks grain coarsening and phase decomposition rather than preserving a nanocrystalline FCC/BCC structure.
No milling speed, duration, ball-to-powder ratio, atmosphere, heating rate, hold time, pressure/displacement-rate constraint, or thermal-expansion constraint is specified.
The indentation experiment cannot distinguish grain-boundary strengthening from solute strengthening; comparison only with the cast baseline does not isolate either mechanism.
The evidence is largely drawn from compositionally different refractory or Al-containing HEAs and does not establish FCC/BCC stability in CoCrFeNiTi.
explanation: The hypothesis captures the broad processing concept and intended FCC-dominant/BCC-minor nanocrystalline product, but mostly restates the requested objective. Its principal operating condition is inconsistent with the target: the relevant SPS regime is approximately 900–1000°C for 10 minutes, whereas 1200–1400°C is supported only by evidence for a different refractory alloy and may promote coarsening. It also omits the target milling regime of 400 rpm, 20:1 ball-to-powder ratio, 1–6 hours under argon, and SPS heating at 50°C/min under vacuum. The mechanism mentions grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening but omits milling-induced lattice strain/dislocation accumulation and does not explain Ti-mediated phase stability or HCP suppression. Outcomes are not quantitative and omit the approximately 83% FCC/17% BCC fraction, sub-48 nm grains, 675 Hv hardness, and 1894 MPa compressive strength. Finally, the proposed 1000 mN/10 s indentation test differs from the target 0.05 kN/15 s protocol and, more importantly, lacks a grain-size-controlled or composition-controlled comparison needed to falsify a grain-refinement mechanism.
